messages:
maria-g: FYI — Customer ACME (prod) escalated a P1: their 'Model Inference Latency (p95, 1m)' alert fired every 1m for ~20m even though the underlying trace/chart shows sparse data and many empty buckets. They say alerts started ~2026-03-16 01:12 UTC.

julie-support: cc @sajid @ian-ops — customer is worried about noise and false positives, billing noticed spike from retries. Provided a screenshot and raw alert payload.

sajid: looking. first thought: aggregation window misalignment between our rollup job and alert rule — we had that bug last quarter. can you paste alert config + example payload?

maria-g: pasted below from support ticket (redacted ids):

```
alert_rule: latency_p95_1m
condition: p95(latency_ms) > 300
window: 1m
evaluation_periods: 1
metric_query: metrics.inference.latency_ms{model:specialized} | rollup(60s, p95)
```

alert-bot: :rotating_light: alert fired 2026-03-16T01:12:00Z - rule latency_p95_1m - value: Infinity (no data buckets)

ian-ops: "value: Infinity (no data buckets)" looks like our sentinel for empty rollup windows. If the rollup returns NaN/Infinity we currently treat it as > threshold. Bug.

sajid: repro steps I ran in staging: create a synthetic meter that emits points at 1:00:05, 1:00:35 then pause. Dashboard rollups (aligned to floor) produced buckets [1:00:00-1:01:00] with partial coverage; our rollup job uses timestamp_trunc to floor to 60s, but alert eval uses sliding window anchored to evaluation time. mismatch leads to empty bucket at eval boundary.

ian-ops: repro query I used (ES-like):
```
POST /metrics/_search
{
  "query": { ... },
  "aggs": {
    "per_minute": { "date_histogram": { "field": "@timestamp", "fixed_interval": "60s", "offset": "0s" },
      "aggs": { "p95": { "percentiles": { "field": "latency_ms", "percents": [95] } } }
    }
  }
}
```

ian-ops: if offset != evaluation anchor (we anchor to eval_ts - 60s) then you can get an empty histogram bucket returned for the evaluated interval. Our alert engine treated missing p95 as Infinity.

julie-support: customer says this started after the 2026-03-15 console deploy. Deploy notes mentioned a change to histogram alignment.

maria-g: asked customer for exact eval timestamps and gave them our sanity checklist. They provided an alert payload showing eval_ts: 2026-03-16T01:12:30Z and rollup window start 01:11:30Z -> 01:12:30Z but the chart buckets are 01:12:00-01:13:00.

sajid: root cause hypothesized: dashboards use floor-aligned 60s buckets, alert eval uses sliding window [t-1m, t) and our rollup engine sometimes returns an empty bucket when the window doesn't fully cover a floored interval. Then alerting code interprets empty -> Infinity.

ian-ops: mitigation options:
- short term: change alert evaluator to treat empty/NaN as "no data" and not fire (or require at least 1 sample)
- medium: harmonize rollup alignment logic so both dashboard and alert engine use same bucketing anchor (prefer eval anchor)
- long term: expose bucket alignment config in Console per-metric

julie-support: customer asked for immediate suppression. Can we set a temporary rule to silence that alert for ACME org for 1h?

sajid: yes — can add a silence on the alert router for org:acme, duration 1h. doing that now.

alert-bot: silence created by sajid for latency_p95_1m org:acme until 2026-03-16T02:13:00Z :white_check_mark:

maria-g: next steps assigned:
- sajid: create a quick patch to make evaluator treat empty/NaN as no-data (hotfix) and push to staging for QA (ETA 2h)
- ian-ops: write an integration test covering mismatched bucket anchors + update rollout notes (ETA EOD)
- julie-support: confirm with ACME that silence mitigates noise and escalate to their SREs if they want more config visibility

sajid: patch drafted, unit tested locally. main change: replace Infinity coercion with null and add has_data flag. Pushing PR link: https://git.redwood/PR/1234

ian-ops: added test vectors and a small doc snippet about rollup anchors to infra-runbook.

julie-support: ACME confirmed noise stopped after silence. They're happy for now but want a status update tomorrow.

maria-g: marking thread P1 -> resolved workaround in place. Will follow up with release notes and customer postmortem link once patch merges. Thx everyone :pray:
